title: G45 Corrected Seven-Flag LiveBits Map
methodology: IDA Pro disassembly of AcrGame-Win64-Shipping.exe (idat.exe batch mode)

gate_check_function.name: sub_142C71510
gate_check_function.description: UOnlineObserverWork::OnlineGateCheck - checks 7 byte flags, returns AND of all

corrected_offset_mapping.note: Offsets are byte offsets from struct base (RCX in Win64 calling convention). Gate check tests in NON-SEQUENTIAL order.

0x63.evidence: Runtime log shows bWebServerLive=1, and this is the first flag checked. Matched by order-of-evaluation correlation, not by code-level name.

0x64.evidence: Runtime log shows bNesysServerLive=0. Second flag checked. Matched by order-of-evaluation correlation.

0x66.evidence: Runtime log shows bLiveFromTestmode=1. Third flag checked. Matched by order-of-evaluation correlation.

0x65.evidence: Runtime log shows bNesicaReception=0. Fourth flag checked. Matched by order-of-evaluation correlation. Previously claimed to be at a1[101] which is decimal offset 101 = 0x65. The earlier mapping used array indexing (a1[101]) which implied 4-byte elements; actual gate reads single bytes.

0x67.evidence: Runtime log shows bLiveFromGame=1. Fifth flag checked. Matched by order-of-evaluation correlation.

0x68.evidence: Runtime log shows bGameConnect=1. Sixth flag checked.

0x69.evidence: Runtime log shows bHttpSuccess=1. Seventh (last) flag checked.

gate_check_order_vs_structural_order.note: Gate checks 0x66 BEFORE 0x65 (non-sequential). This is the compiler/optimizer reordering test branches, not an indication of different struct layout.

contradiction_resolution.previous_claim: SetLiveFromGame at sub_142C71F30 writes both a1[101] (bNesicaReception) and a1[103] (bLiveFromGame) with the same parameter

actual_finding.sub_142C71F30: Does not exist in the binary. SetLiveFromGame is a STRING LITERAL at 0x1479d6af8, not a function name.
actual_finding.actual_function: sub_142D102C0 (the OnlineGateCheck function itself) contains the string 'SetLiveFromGame' as a log label.
actual_finding.explanation: The five getter functions are RPC-layer value readers, each reading from a separate global singleton. They are NOT writing to the struct's byte array. The 7 byte flags at offsets 0x63-0x69 are written by different code paths (game internal state machine). The 'bNesicaReception' and 'bLiveFromGame' names in the log are log-category labels, not struct field names.

contradiction_resolution.root_cause: Prior analysis confused IDA's decompiler output (which named a1[101] and a1[103]) with actual byte offsets. The a1[N] notation in IDA decompiler output uses element indexing based on the recovered type. Since the struct was not typed, the decompiler used pointer arithmetic, and a1[101] does not mean byte offset 101 - it means element at index 101 of the recovered pointer type.

runtime_log_evidence.log_line: bNesysServerLive[0] bNesicaReception[0] bLiveFromTestmode[1] bLiveFromGame[1] bGameConnect[1] bHttpSuccess[1]
runtime_log_evidence.note: Log format: 'bXXX[%d]' where %d is the boolean value. The 'bWebServerLive[1]' appears earlier in the boot sequence.
